name: Sore Loser
why: Steals 3 followers from the leader only when you won nothing; the leader can see it coming, a fair catch-up.

name: Walk-In
why: A blind draw from the pile is a fun gamble, and every rival gets a red as a gift.

name: Loyalists
why: Quiet protection for your other members; fine, no moment.

name: Trendsetters
why: Shop churn on each recruit; useful, rarely a felt moment.

name: Spoilsport
why: At round end the leader of a contest just loses it with no way to answer; the victim feels robbed of a win they earned.

name: Body Snatchers
why: Even-cost swap each round; the rival loses a chosen member but gets one of equal cost back.

name: Lie Low
why: Small steal plus a round of safety; fine.

name: Heist
why: A clean 3-follower steal; stings but it is an open space rivals can see and take first.

name: Echo
why: Reading the table to copy the last action is a satisfying little timing puzzle.

name: Shoplifter
why: A 1-resource nibble per recruit; victims shrug it off.

name: Panel
why: Recruiting it also upgrades another member; a pleasant two-for-one moment.

name: Demote
why: Trades down with a rival who still gets your member back; mild sting, decent tempo.

name: Doormen
why: Every round it sends a rival's chosen member away and can hand them a worse one; the same victim is singled out repeatedly with no answer, before round III.

name: Agents
why: Passive copy block; fine, no moment.

name: Potluck
why: Rivals pick what to give and get 2 silver back; a sting nobody minds.

name: Mob
why: A big round-end payoff for dominating red feels great to land.

name: Philanthropist
why: Gifts silver to rivals for followers; a gift that pays the owner.

name: Sample
why: Borrowing a rival's best On Recruit is a clever, fun moment.

name: Old Maid
why: A hot potato: no fun to receive, but everyone knows it is out there and can dodge it.

name: Raiders
why: Once-per-game 4-follower steal with 2 white paid back; a fair sting.

name: Crunch Time
why: Two turns in a row is a powerful, satisfying burst.

name: Debt Collectors
why: Once-per-game 2 silver from each rival; small and shrugged off.

name: Grifter
why: Scaling steal on recruit; fine.

name: Farewell
why: Cashing out a member for followers is a solid, quiet play.

name: Bury
why: Denies a shop member and pays some blue; fine.

name: High Society
why: Followers trickle in as rivals use silver; fine.

name: Spree
why: Three recruits in one turn is a big round III moment.

name: Fan Club
why: Copying the leader's action on recruit is a fun catch-up surprise.

name: Overtime
why: An extra minion in the last round feels powerful.

name: Tribute Band
why: Doing every action a rival took is a huge, memorable turn.

name: Window Shopper
why: Shop cycling with small resource gains; fine.

name: Early Birds
why: Passive skip immunity; fine.

name: Impersonator
why: Choosing a rival's ability to wear each round is fun to play.

name: Window Dressers
why: A one-time shop wipe on a cheap 3-count body; fine.

name: Largesse
why: A big gift to rivals that turns into followers for you.

name: Party Crasher
why: Jumping onto a taken space is a fun surprise moment.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Reading where rivals sit for a resource haul; fine.

name: Poach
why: Taking a chosen member hurts, but only in round III and from an open space.

name: Martyrs
why: Losing it pays you, so being stolen from becomes a win; fun twist.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: A free extra recruit on arrival feels generous and strong.

name: Help Yourself
why: A split steal; rivals take small, spread-out hits.

name: Meddler
why: Swapping one of each rival's resources is a mild nuisance; fine.

name: Line Cutters
why: Always going first is useful but quiet.

name: Creditor
why: Takes 2 followers from a chosen rival each round but pays them 3 silver; fair.

name: Bouncers
why: Skipping two rivals once is a nice tempo hit that victims recover from.

name: Customs Officer
why: Passive payback against steals; fine.

name: Savings
why: Blue plus a shop nudge; fine.

name: Cutpurse
why: A 1-resource nibble at the richest rival each round; shrugged off.

name: Double Agent
why: You take whichever rival member you want and hand them a 1-follower card, before round III; the victim feels robbed.

name: Guest of Honor
why: Giving a rival a cheap member for 4 followers is a gift both sides like.

name: Debutantes
why: Doubling your silver is a big moment and rivals get silver too.

name: Night Watch
why: Followers when rivals go last; fine.

name: Accomplice
why: A cheap 3-resource steal; small sting.

name: Scavenger
why: Grabbing what rivals send away is a nice snipe, rarely big.

name: Last Call
why: Cashing saved minions for followers is a satisfying payoff.

name: Toast
why: A big silver haul that gifts rivals too.

name: Initiation
why: A free member up to 8 in round III feels great.

name: Godparent
why: Handing a rival a member for followers is a gift with a payoff.

name: Deprogrammers
why: A cheap rider on member steals; fine.

name: Right Away
why: A quick extra turn; fine.

name: Hostesses
why: Gifting silver every round for followers; a gift rivals welcome.

name: Fence
why: Passive payback when robbed; fine.

name: Con Men
why: A big 5-resource steal; it stings but it is resources, not members.

name: Extortionist
why: Repeated 2-resource hits on the richest rival, who can see it coming and spend down.

name: Closer
why: A purple bonus for going last; fine.

name: Hot Streak
why: Chaining turns into a burst of followers is a fun combo moment.

name: Second-Story Man
why: A pre-contest steal that can swing magenta; fine.

name: Bodyguards
why: Steal immunity; quiet but fair.

name: Tryout
why: Using a shop member's effect without buying it is a clever, fun play.

name: Night Owls
why: A bonus minion after your last feels powerful.

name: Housewarming
why: A free member up to 5 is a satisfying round II grab.
